title: Perfect Divisibility, Linear Divisibility and Chair-Free Graphs
summary: A graph is perfectly divisible if every induced subgraph with at least one edge admits a partition into a perfect induced subgraph and an induced subgraph with smaller clique number. Every perfectly divisible graph $G$ satisfies $χ(H)\leq\binom{ω(H)+1}{2}$ for every induced subgraph $H$ of $G$. We show that the converse fails: for every non-negative integer $t$, the graph $P(17)\vee K_t$ satisfies this bound for every induced subgraph but is not perfectly divisible, yielding an infinite family of counterexamples.
